Apple's annual September event is just around the corner, and three brand-new iPhone models are expected to be unveiled: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's a roundup of what we know so far.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be the successors to Apple's popular 17 Pro lineup.

Rumoured new features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, delivering simultaneous gains in performance and efficiency
  • A major camera system upgrade, headlined by a main lens with a variable aperture
  • The Dynamic Island shrinks by 35%, giving the design a more modern look
  • A bold new colour joins the lineup, with a deep burgundy taking centre stage
  • The best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing particularly significant gains
  • A redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite connectivity features, including 5G satellite communication

The starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to rise. Market estimates put it at around US$1,399, though I expect the actual pricing to be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to be Apple's first foldable iPhone, priced above US$2,000, carving out an entirely new premium tier.

This foldable design will make the iPhone Ultra Apple's most groundbreaking model to date. The device adopts a wide book-style folding form factor, with an outer display of roughly 5.4 inches and an inner display of around 7.8 inches, delivering an experience similar to the iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to follow the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame for a clean, minimalist aesthetic.

The iPhone Ultra will sport two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) and two front cameras to serve the inner and outer displays. Authentication will rely on Touch ID rather than Face ID.

Software will be the biggest highlight of this new device. Powered by iOS 27, it will support split-view multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts tailored to the foldable form factor, perfectly complementing the fresh hardware design.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, featuring the same A20 Pro chip, along with a vapour chamber cooling system and the C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, the September event is also expected to see the launch of the new entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest that Apple will significantly revamp its autumn lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this is purely a strategic move or a forced response to tight memory supply. Either way, with the more affordable models sitting this one out, this autumn's iPhone lineup will be squarely focused on the high-end market.
